newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Shevardnadze to veto arming of parliament members.
newsitem.headline: Shevardnadze to veto arming of parliament members.

text.p: Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze has pledged to veto a parliamentary bill giving lawmakers the right to carry firearms for life, his office said on Tuesday.
Parliament last week voted by an overwhelming margin to give members the right to carry pistols and other non-automatic firearms even after they have left office.

"I think that an armed parliament, and moreover letting parliament members carry weapons even after their terms have ended, is not acceptable for a democratic country," the press service reported him as telling a cabinet meeting late on Monday.
"This is a case where the president has the right to exercise a veto."

Under a lapsed 1994 law, parliament members were allowed lifetime rights to carry weapons in the volatile former Soviet republic, which was torn by several civil and ethnic conflicts after the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991.
Opponents had argued that this, justified at the time by the chaos in Georgia, was no longer necessary.

But supporters of the measure said that parliament members involved in corruption investigation committees and other sensitive activities were at risk of attack and that they should therefore be allowed firearms.
